description: If the price of a good rises what happens to the quantity demanded according to the law of demand?
explanation: The law of demand states that price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions. A price rise reduces quantity demanded.

description: What causes a rightward shift in the demand curve?
explanation: A demand curve shifts right when consumers are willing to buy more at every price. Higher income for a normal good causes this.
choice0: A rise in the good's own price
choice1: A fall in consumer income for a normal good
choice2: An increase in consumer income for a normal good

description: A good with price elasticity of demand equal to -2 is best described as:
explanation: An elasticity magnitude greater than 1 means quantity demanded changes by a larger percentage than price - this is elastic demand.

description: A student can either attend college earning \$50000 more per year in future wages or work immediately at \$30000 per year. What is the opportunity cost of attending college?
explanation: The opportunity cost is the best alternative given up. Working immediately at \$30000 per year is what the student foregoes.

description: Which expenditure component of GDP is typically the largest in the United States?
explanation: Consumer spending (C) is consistently the largest component of GDP in the US typically accounting for about two-thirds of total output.

description: If the CPI rises from 100 to 108 what is the inflation rate?
explanation: Inflation rate = (new CPI - old CPI) / old CPI x 100 = (108 - 100) / 100 x 100 = 8%.

description: In perfect competition each firm is a:
explanation: In a perfectly competitive market no single firm can influence the market price. Each firm takes the market price as given and is a price taker.

description: An increase in government spending with no change in taxes is an example of:
explanation: Expansionary fiscal policy involves increasing government spending or cutting taxes (or both) to stimulate economic activity.

description: When the central bank raises interest rates what is the likely effect on investment spending?
explanation: Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive so businesses reduce investment spending on new capital.

description: Country A can produce 10 cars or 20 tons of wheat. Country B can produce 5 cars or 15 tons of wheat. What is Country A's opportunity cost of one car?
explanation: To produce 1 car Country A gives up 20 / 10 = 2 tons of wheat. Country B gives up 15 / 5 = 3 tons per car. A has comparative advantage in cars.
hint: Opp. cost of 1 car = wheat / cars

description: What happens to the equilibrium price when supply decreases and demand stays constant?
explanation: A decrease in supply shifts the supply curve left. With unchanged demand this raises the equilibrium price.

description: Which of the following goods is likely to have highly inelastic demand?
explanation: Insulin is a necessity for diabetics with few or no substitutes. Its demand is highly inelastic - consumers must buy it regardless of price.

description: What does a firm maximize in the standard economic model?
explanation: In the standard economic model firms are assumed to maximize profit defined as total revenue minus total cost.

description: Which of the following best describes a recession?
explanation: A recession is conventionally defined as two or more consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth.
choice0: A period of rapid economic growth
choice1: Two or more consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth
choice2: A decrease in the unemployment rate
choice3: A rise in the inflation rate above 5%

description: What is the effect of a tariff on imported goods?
explanation: A tariff raises the price of imports causing domestic consumers to pay more while protecting domestic producers from foreign competition.
choice0: It lowers the price of imports for consumers
choice1: It increases the volume of imported goods
choice2: It raises the price of imports protecting domestic producers

description: What is consumer surplus?
explanation: Consumer surplus is the difference between the maximum price a consumer is willing to pay and the price they actually pay.
choice0: Willingness to pay minus actual price paid
choice1: The profit earned by a firm
choice2: The area under the supply curve
choice3: The difference between price and marginal cost

description: Average total cost is calculated as:
explanation: Average total cost (ATC) equals total cost divided by quantity produced. It represents the cost per unit of output.
choice1: Fixed cost divided by variable cost

description: Why does a market with a negative externality tend to overproduce the good?
explanation: When producers do not bear the full social cost of production (e.g. pollution) the good is produced in excess of the socially optimal quantity.
choice1: Because private cost is lower than social cost so firms overproduce

description: Real GDP differs from nominal GDP because real GDP:
explanation: Real GDP is adjusted for changes in the price level (inflation). It measures actual output growth by removing price effects.
choice2: Is adjusted for inflation to reflect real output
choice3: Counts both final and intermediate goods

description: What is stagflation?
explanation: Stagflation is a combination of stagnant economic growth (high unemployment) and high inflation occurring at the same time - difficult for policymakers to address.
choice0: High inflation combined with slow growth or high unemployment
choice1: A rapid and sustained fall in prices
choice2: High growth combined with low inflation
choice3: Inflation caused only by supply shocks

description: Which market structure is characterized by many firms selling slightly differentiated products?
explanation: Monopolistic competition features many firms each selling products that are slightly different from rivals. Examples include restaurants and clothing brands.

description: Which of the following is an example of an automatic stabilizer?
explanation: Unemployment insurance automatically pays out more when the economy weakens without needing new legislation - it is an automatic stabilizer.

description: Quantitative easing involves a central bank:
explanation: Quantitative easing (QE) is when a central bank buys large amounts of assets such as government bonds to inject money into the economy and lower long-term interest rates.
choice0: Raising the reserve requirement for banks
choice2: Buying large quantities of assets to inject money into the economy

description: Which of the following statements about comparative advantage is true?
explanation: Comparative advantage depends on opportunity cost not absolute productivity. A country should specialize in the good where its opportunity cost is lowest.
choice0: A country should produce goods where its opportunity cost is lowest
choice1: A country must have absolute advantage to gain from trade
choice2: A larger country always has comparative advantage

description: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that:
explanation: As a consumer eats more of a good the additional satisfaction (marginal utility) from each extra unit decreases after a point.
choice0: Total utility always decreases as consumption rises
choice2: More income always increases utility by a constant amount
choice3: Each additional unit consumed adds less utility than the previous one

description: A price floor set above the equilibrium price leads to:
explanation: A price floor above equilibrium prevents prices from falling to equilibrium. More is supplied than demanded creating a surplus.

description: In the short run which of the following is a variable cost for a typical manufacturing firm?
explanation: Raw materials vary directly with output level making them a variable cost. Rent is fixed regardless of output.
choice3: Interest payments on a long-term loan

description: If two goods are substitutes an increase in the price of good A will:
explanation: Substitute goods compete for the same consumer need. If A's price rises consumers switch to B increasing demand for B.
choice2: Have no effect on demand for good B

description: Which of the following transactions would be included in GDP?
explanation: GDP counts final goods and services produced domestically. A new laptop sold to a household is a final consumer good.
choice0: A homeowner selling their old sofa to a neighbor (used good)
choice1: The purchase of existing shares of stock
choice2: A transfer payment such as a Social Security check
choice3: A new laptop computer sold to a student

description: Which group tends to be hurt most by unexpected inflation?
explanation: Creditors (lenders) who are owed fixed dollar amounts in the future are hurt because inflation erodes the real value of those repayments.

description: Which of the following is a barrier to entry in a monopoly market?
explanation: A patent grants an exclusive right to produce a product preventing competitors from entering and maintaining monopoly power.
choice2: A patent giving exclusive rights to produce a product

description: What does a trade deficit mean for a country?
explanation: A trade deficit means a country imports more than it exports - the value of imports exceeds the value of exports in a given period.
choice0: A country imports more than it exports
choice1: A country exports more than it imports

description: What happens to consumer surplus when price falls?
explanation: A lower price means consumers pay less than their willingness to pay for more units. Consumer surplus increases.

description: What is a shift in supply versus a movement along the supply curve?
explanation: A change in price causes movement along the supply curve. A change in factors like technology or input costs shifts the entire curve.
choice0: Both are caused by price changes
choice1: A price change moves along the curve; other factors shift the curve
choice2: A shift is caused by a change in price
choice3: A movement is caused by a change in consumer income

description: A country that specializes in producing goods where it has comparative advantage and trades is applying which economic concept?
explanation: This describes the theory of comparative advantage and the gains from trade. Countries benefit by specializing and trading.
choice2: Comparative advantage and gains from trade

description: What is the multiplier effect in fiscal policy?
explanation: The multiplier effect means that an initial increase in government spending leads to a larger total increase in GDP because spending by one becomes income for another.
choice0: An initial spending increase leads to a larger total increase in GDP
choice1: Government must raise taxes when it increases spending
choice2: Interest rates automatically rise after fiscal stimulus
choice3: The central bank matches any fiscal expansion

description: A decrease in the money supply tends to:
explanation: Reducing the money supply raises interest rates which discourages borrowing investment and spending leading to a decrease in inflation and output.
choice0: Lower interest rates and stimulate growth
choice1: Have no effect on interest rates
choice2: Increase inflation in the short run
choice3: Raise interest rates and reduce spending

description: When average total cost is falling as output increases marginal cost is:
explanation: When MC is below ATC pulling the average down ATC is declining. This is a standard relationship between marginal and average cost.

description: Which of the following would make demand for a good more inelastic?
explanation: Demand is more inelastic when there are fewer substitutes when the good is a necessity or when it takes a small share of income.
choice3: The good being a luxury item

description: What government policy is commonly used to correct a negative externality?
explanation: A Pigouvian tax is a tax equal to the external cost that forces producers to internalize costs they would otherwise impose on third parties.
choice0: A tax equal to the external cost (Pigouvian tax)
choice2: A subsidy to producers of the good

description: GDP per capita is used as a measure of:
explanation: GDP per capita (GDP divided by population) is a widely used proxy for the average standard of living in a country.
choice3: Average living standards in a country

description: The natural rate of unemployment includes which types of unemployment?
explanation: The natural rate includes frictional (between jobs) and structural (skill mismatch) unemployment but not cyclical unemployment.

description: When a consumer's budget constraint shifts outward it means:
explanation: An outward shift in the budget constraint means the consumer can afford more of both goods typically because income has risen or prices have fallen.
choice0: Prices of both goods have risen
choice1: Tastes have changed toward cheaper goods
choice2: Income has risen or prices have fallen allowing more consumption
choice3: The government has imposed a price ceiling

description: What is the purpose of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
explanation: The WTO facilitates international trade by providing a forum for negotiating trade agreements and resolving trade disputes between member countries.
choice0: To regulate international trade rules and resolve trade disputes
choice2: To provide development loans to poor countries
choice3: To impose tariffs on behalf of member nations

description: What does producer surplus represent?
explanation: Producer surplus is the difference between the price a producer receives and the minimum price they would have accepted (their marginal cost).
choice0: The cost of producing each unit
choice1: The difference between consumer willingness to pay and price
choice2: Total revenue earned by the firm
choice3: The difference between market price and the minimum price a seller accepts

description: Why do natural monopolies exist?
explanation: Natural monopolies occur when a single firm can supply the entire market at a lower average cost than multiple competing firms due to very high fixed costs.
choice0: Because the government grants them a legal right to monopolize
choice1: Because average costs keep falling so one firm can serve the market cheapest
choice2: Because they produce goods with no substitutes
choice3: Because they engage in predatory pricing

description: Which of the following best describes demand-pull inflation?
explanation: Demand-pull inflation occurs when aggregate demand in the economy exceeds aggregate supply causing prices to be pulled upward.
choice0: Inflation caused by rising production costs
choice1: Inflation caused by supply chain disruptions
choice2: Inflation caused by excess aggregate demand relative to supply
choice3: Inflation caused by falling consumer confidence

description: Diminishing returns to labor means that as more workers are added to a fixed amount of capital:
explanation: The law of diminishing returns states that adding more of a variable input to a fixed input eventually reduces the marginal product of that variable input.
choice0: Each additional worker adds less to total output than the previous one

description: A contractionary fiscal policy would include:
explanation: Contractionary fiscal policy reduces aggregate demand by cutting government spending or raising taxes to slow inflation.
choice2: Creating a new unemployment insurance program
choice3: Raising taxes to reduce the government budget deficit

description: If a country has comparative advantage in producing wheat it should:
explanation: Comparative advantage guides specialization. The country should specialize in wheat production and trade for other goods.
choice0: Produce equal amounts of wheat and all other goods
choice1: Specialize in wheat production and trade for other goods
choice2: Impose tariffs to protect all other domestic industries
choice3: Focus on achieving absolute advantage in all goods
